name: Higgs mechanism: fermion and W, Z rest masses proportional to phi (m -> m phi/v) -- Morrissey & Ramsey-Musolf 1206.2942 p.4

source.located: arXiv:1206.2942v1 [hep-ph], 13 Jun 2012, D. E. Morrissey (TRIUMF) and M. J. Ramsey-Musolf (Wisconsin/Caltech), 'Electroweak baryogenesis' (review, NPAC-12-08). The sentence is Sec. 2 'The electroweak phase transition', p.4, immediately below eq. (1).

published_statement: p.4: 'The transition from symmetric to broken phase in the SM can be characterized by the vacuum expectation value (VEV) of the Higgs field H = (H+, H0)^T that transforms as (1, 2, 1/2) under SU(3)c x SU(2)L x U(1)Y. A field basis can always be chosen such that only the real component of H0 develops a non-zero expectation value. Thus, we will write  phi/sqrt(2) = <H0> . (1)  The symmetric phase corresponds to phi = 0 and the broken phase to phi != 0. Note that (in unitary gauge) the masses of the W+- and Z0 weak vector bosons and the fermions are proportional to phi.'
published_hypotheses: Standard Model: one Higgs doublet H ~ (1,2,1/2); 'in the SM' is the sentence's frame (p.4)
phi is the (homogeneous) vacuum expectation value, phi/sqrt(2) = <H0>, basis chosen so only Re H0 has a vev (eq. 1)

Implicit, never stated: tree level / renormalisable Yukawa couplings, so m_f = y_f phi/sqrt(2). The review itself warns (p.8) that 'the vacuum expectation value of the one-loop effective potential phi at any temperature is gauge-dependent', so beyond tree level phi is not a physical quantity by itself
Implicit: 'the fermions' means the SM fermions with Dirac masses from Yukawas (neutrino masses are not discussed anywhere in the pages read)

Convention note (not a hypothesis): eq. (1) makes phi = sqrt(2)<H0> ~ 246 GeV, while eq. (20) p.9 uses v(0) = 174 GeV = <H0>. Two normalisations in one paper; not an error, but a reader mixing them errs by sqrt(2). The tree uses 246.22 GeV (phi-normalisation), consistently with eq. (1).

lacked_data: What the authors lacked: in June 2012 (three weeks before the discovery) they had no Higgs boson, no Higgs mass and no coupling measurement of any kind; the sentence is a structural remark about the SM Lagrangian, not an inference from data. What came later: the discovery, then ATLAS/CMS coupling maps (2207.00092) that CONFIRM kappa = 1 (m proportional to phi) for W, Z (~5 %) and t, b, tau (~7-12 %), with muon evidence emerging. Does having it change the conclusion? For the statement as published (SM, unitary gauge, tree level): no -- nothing measured contradicts it and the re-derivation agrees. For the tree's use on the payload's fermions e, u, d: the data the authors lacked are STILL lacking. kappa_e is bounded only to |kappa_e| < 262 and kappa_e = 0 is not excluded by the H->ee search; first-generation quark Yukawas are assumed, not measured, in the ATLAS combination. So M's hypothesis holds in a precise, narrow sense: not that the 2012 statement is wrong, but that the tree's 'm_e is 100% Higgs, subtract exactly 1' (address.py:514) and 'which is what the Higgs gives the fermions' (excite.py:145-147) rest on an SM prediction for exactly the particles no experiment has yet tested. Evidence against over-reading this: every Yukawa that HAS been measured agrees with kappa = 1, and simplified models allowing large kappa_e require fine-tuned cancellations (2501.07628 p.5). Evidence for caution: 2501.07628 exhibits models consistent with all current data with kappa_e ~ 265-925. Which tree conclusions move: K_mu (one-for-one in kappa_e) and the stable-matter f under H2 (proportional to kappa_l); which do not: massform C5/D27 (m(0) = 0 survives any single-doublet m(phi)) and C2's 3.010e-4 share.
grade_evidence: The published statement is READ verbatim (1206.2942v1 p.4, matching the tree's held text at massform.py:1133-1135) and re-derived at tree level by sympy (m_W = g phi/2, m_Z = sqrt(g^2+g'^2) phi/2, m_f = y phi/sqrt2, all d ln m/d ln phi = 1; 29/29 checks pass). No datum has moved against it and the confirmed Yukawas (t, b, tau, W, Z) agree. It is NOT WRONG and nothing is refuted. It is NARROWED as the tree uses it because two hypotheses the source carries implicitly are dropped at named sites: (i) the renormalisable-SM relation kappa_f = 1 for e, u, d -- asserted as fact at excite.py:145-147 and address.py:514 ('m_e is 100% Higgs, so subtract exactly 1'), whereas check C proves kappa_f = d ln m_f/d ln phi is the LHC coupling modifier and the data bound kappa_e only to |kappa_e| < 262 (ATLAS 1909.10235, computed) and assume kappa_u, kappa_d (2207.00092 p.8); (ii) a single Higgs doublet, unnamed, on which massform's contrapositive 'm_f > 0 => phi != 0' (massform.py:212) rests. The tree's own H-TREE (massform.py:751) correctly adds tree level. The massform/ledger uses that need only m(0) = 0 (C5, D27, C2) survive any single-doublet m(phi) (check D) and STAND on H-TREE plus the unnamed single-doublet premise; the linear uses (address.K_mu; excite D20 for an electron-borne source; the S part of f) hold on the smaller class kappa = 1, which is a prediction untested for the payload's fermions. Not graded DATA-DEPENDENT because no datum has moved or is contested: kappa_e, kappa_u, kappa_d are unmeasured, not in tension.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree names H-SM (one doublet, renormalisable Yukawas, kappa_e = kappa_u = kappa_d = 1, measured only to |kappa_e| < 262 and assumed for u, d) at excite.py:145-147 and address.py:514 and carries it into K_mu and D20's f; or a measurement (FCC-ee Higgs-pole run, projected |y_e| < 1.6 y_SM; light-quark Yukawa probes) finds kappa_e, kappa_u, kappa_d consistent with 1. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a measured kappa_e or kappa_l different from 1, or a contested one -- then K_mu and the H2 stable-matter density move (checks G2, G3). To WRONG: only a measured non-SM kappa for a payload fermion together with the tree continuing to assert 'exactly 1'; nothing of the kind exists. The published SM statement itself could change only if the SM Lagrangian were not the one nature uses for these fermions.
